newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-Canada open skies pact a success - American.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Canada open skies pact a success - American.

text.p: A two-year open skies agreement between the United States and Canada has been a "huge success," American Airlines President Donald Carty said Tuesday.

"If you add it all up, and when you look at the two-year report card of the U.S.-Canadian open skies agreement, the grade has clearly got to be an A-plus," Carty said at a luncheon sponsored by the Canadian-American Business Council.

Carty said the agreement, which removes restrictions on air traffic across the Canadian-U.S. border, has been a boon for business and consumers with increased trade opportunities, more convenient and direct flights and lower fares due to increased competition.
Carty said the U.S.-Canada pact is serving as an example to encourage other countries to develop similar agreements.

"The key element of every carrier's future is its ability to serve as many different markets around the world as possible," he said. "It won't happen overnight, but I believe as long as we continue to provide an example of how it can work, the rest of the world won't be far behind."
The open skies agreement between the United States and Canada was approved in February 1995 and is in its last stages of implementation.
